structure.title: Prologue and parodos · A blind traveller sits down
structure.text: Guided by Antigone, Oedipus rests in a sacred grove. The locals want him off the ground before they even discover his name. A man long treated as a danger to any host must find someone willing to hear his petition.

structure.title: First episode – fourth stasimon · Rival claims upon an exile
structure.text: News from Thebes turns an unwanted old man into a desirable political asset. His sons, Creon and the ruler of Athens stand in different relations to the body everyone suddenly wants to possess. Oedipus still has a choice about where he belongs.

people.name: Oedipus
people.role: A blind exile at the end of his wandering
people.text: Old and dependent on his daughter's arm, he stops in a grove outside Athens that he recognises as the place foretold for his death. He insists that what he did, he did in ignorance, and he now holds something rulers want.

people.name: Antigone and Ismene
people.role: Daughters doing different kinds of work
people.text: Antigone has walked beside her father. Ismene brings intelligence from home. Their practical knowledge of his needs stands beside the grand claims now being made on his loyalty.

people.name: Theseus
people.text: His offer of protection has a practical meaning when another ruler turns up prepared to take people by force. Athens is being judged by the welcome it gives a frightened stranger.

prerequisites.title: Sophocles' Oedipus Rex
prerequisites.text: Oedipus arrives at Colonus old, blind and in exile because of what he discovered in the earlier play. Colonus keeps returning to those discoveries and to the question of his guilt, so Oedipus Rex gives it its weight.

context.title: The grove at Colonus
context.text: Sacred ground has rules about who may enter and how a trespass can be repaired. The chorus's first alarm is local knowledge. It takes time for the citizens to see what sort of stranger has broken the rule.

notice.text: Listen to the verbs for leading someone.
notice.why: At first Oedipus depends on his daughter for every unfamiliar step. Changes in who directs a journey register a change in his authority long before anyone gives it a name.

notice.text: Who asks forgiveness, and what else do they need?
notice.why: Appeals to kinship arrive alongside urgent political business. Oedipus remembers precisely when that same kinship failed to secure him a bed or a home.

opening: An old blind man arrives outside Athens with his daughter, looking for somewhere he can sit without being driven away. His name is Oedipus, and the people who hear it want him gone. Yet the exile whom nobody wishes to shelter is suddenly valuable to the rulers who once abandoned him. Sophocles returns to a ruined king whose remaining power lies in deciding whom to trust, and who refuses to let other people turn his suffering into an asset without his consent.
